did_you_know.text: The word "nissah" means “tested” here, not harmed or tempted. Abraham’s reply, “Here I am,” expresses readiness to listen and respond.
The land called “the land of Moriah” is mentioned again in 2 Chronicles as the place where the Temple was built in Jerusalem. Genesis itself, however, does not give the mountain’s exact location.
The journey lasts three days, and only then does Abraham see the place from a distance. In the Bible, a period of three days often marks preparation for or transition to an important event.

Isaac carries the wood for the offering, while Abraham carries the fire and the knife. The description shows that each has a role in the preparations, although the boy does not yet know the whole picture.
The phrase “God will see to it” can literally mean that God will see or find the lamb; in traditional translation it is also understood as “God will provide the lamb.”
When the angel calls “Abraham, Abraham,” the repeated name usually marks an urgent and important call in the Bible. Abraham again answers, “Here I am,” as he did at the beginning of the story.
The name “The LORD will see” comes from the root r-ʾ-h, so it can also be understood as “The LORD will provide.” This wordplay is connected to the ram found there instead of Isaac.
Rebekah appears here for the first time, before the story introduces her directly. She is Nahor’s granddaughter and Bethuel’s daughter, and later becomes Isaac’s wife.
